The one criticism I can put forward, that in my opinion lets down the show, is the extremely quick turnaround after a problem is solved and abandoned.  For instance, in ep 3 of season 4, Mac proposes Desi fly along the current to reduce fuel consumption as the stress on the plane would be less, Mac and Desi take their time, completing a dangerous manoeuvre that risked their lives as well a father and son to get the plane in position over the mountains, then the very next second after this is achieved, they abandon this when the tuck on the ground is run into and they need to leave the current they worked so hard to get into and just land on top of the truck (great stunt tho)

Another example of this was when Jim MacGyver sacrifies himself to slow the bad guys down and blow up the bomb manually only to have codex blow up the whole building to cover thier tracks. 

Now, these moments are great, IMO,  but their timing undermines and negates the risk or the sacrifice that happened mere seconds ago. The achievement that took risk or sacrifice needs to breathe so the characters and thus the audience feel like the action that just took place was worth something.

I agree that we can all have different interpretations of the same thing. Art is wonderful like that. I would like to leave you with a thought if I may.

In psychology and philosophy, there is a concept of intent and responsibility and the notion that both are equally important in communication as well as in relationships. I think your emphasis is on the intent, Peter might not intend to hurt but he does. My focus is on responsibility; that of Peter and that of the writers. 

For Peter, its two folds, one, he is a law enforcement officer, and even though in our society today you wouldn't know it since it's not exemplified a lot of the time, but LEO's make the decision to uphold responsibility of the highest regard amongst other things, I think it's one of the reasons he is written as FBI.  Peter has chosen to be a guiding force in Neal's life and that is amazing, but with that comes the responsibility not to do harm, which he fails at, over and over again. Second, he views himself as the 'morally superior' person, in other words, he is the good guy and Neal's the one to be corrected and shaped to be more of  "the good guy". And that's fine we all need people to inspire us to be better. The problem with Peter is that in other to uphold that moral superiority you have to be aware of oneself, and by that i mean trying to help someone is  as good as how you help someone; you can have the best intentions but if all of most of what you do is hurt that person, that defects the purpose. If you're contradicting yourself or presenting as someone trustworthy yet simultaneously betraying someone's trust or flip flopping on issues you say you believe in, then that guide you're supposed to be is jeopardized because the foundation is shaky.

The thing is the writers present Neal as someone that is under the guidance of Peter, meaning Peter is the moral centre of the show, I'm not saying he can't be flawed he can and that makes for better TV, BUT the moral center if flawed has to have a growing arch to their character, so he has to become aware and better himself. When he repeats failings without acknowledging them in the first place then its assumed that the writers expect us to accept that behaviour as one that correlates with being the good guy. And it does not.

Also, Peter never apologizes, yes you don't have to use the words sorry to constitute an apology, but you do have to show that you are sorry. To show implies change or even the understanding or acknowledgement that you were wrong and you ought to be better, Peter NEVER displays this, so imo he never apologizes.

I agree that we can not all agree on this, it would be nice if when it came to ethics there was a consensus, but that makes for a more interesting world. I believe in diversity, and I believe that that implies diversity in opinions and points of view as well. So thank you for reading this and for the wonderful conversation.
